name: Notion
summary: Self-serve: create a public (OAuth) integration and any workspace can connect immediately - Notion says Marketplace review is not required. The nuance is the permission model: users pick individual pages, so your agent only sees what was shared.
difficulty_reason: No approval step; the main design work is handling page-level sharing in your agent UX.

effort.waiting_on: Nothing - no review required to authorise other workspaces.

bottom_line: Create a public integration in Notion's developer portal with installation scope 'any workspace' (this cannot be changed later). Store both the access and refresh tokens. Design your agent so it tells users to share the right pages in the picker, and offers a re-auth link to add pages later - most 'Notion isn't working' tickets are really 'page not shared'.
app_type: Public integration (OAuth) in the Notion developer portal. Internal integrations (single workspace, static token) are only for your own workspace.

scope_paths.name: Read/write pages and databases the user shares
Read user emails
scopes: Read user information including email addresses
scope_paths.review: None, but shown to the user at consent

scope_paths.name: Notion Marketplace listing
scope_paths.review: Listing review, managed separately under Listings

prerequisites.detail: Use a dedicated workspace for testing so you can control shared pages.
Any workspace vs selected workspaces - cannot be changed after creation.

stages.name: Create the public integration
stages.goal: You have a client ID, client secret and authorisation URL.

steps.title: Create a new integration in the developer portal
steps.detail: Choose the public/OAuth type, set installation scope to 'any workspace', and set capabilities (read/update/insert content, user info).

steps.title: Add redirect URIs
steps.detail: If you register more than one, you must send redirect_uri in the token request.

steps.title: Copy client ID/secret from the Configuration tab

stages.name: Wire up and test
stages.goal: A test workspace is connected and the agent can read a shared page.

steps.title: Implement authorise + token exchange
steps.detail: Authorise at https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize (owner=user); exchange the code at the token endpoint with HTTP Basic auth. Persist access_token, refresh_token, bot_id, workspace_id.

steps.title: Connect and share a page in the picker
steps.detail: Verify the agent sees only shared pages and their children.

steps.title: Test refresh
steps.detail: grant_type=refresh_token returns a new access AND refresh token - store both.

token_facts.value: Token response includes a refresh_token; refreshing returns a new pair
Not stated in the authorisation docs - handle 401 by refreshing
Per-user, per-page: only pages selected in the picker (and their children)

gotchas.title: Installation scope is permanent
gotchas.detail: Choosing 'selected workspaces' by mistake means creating a new integration (new client ID) later.

gotchas.title: Agent sees nothing until pages are shared
gotchas.detail: If a user approves but doesn't finish the flow, or picks no pages, the integration has no access. Build an empty-state that sends them back through the picker.

gotchas.title: Per-user authorisations
gotchas.detail: Each user authorises separately and only that user's shared pages are reachable via their token.

blockers.symptom: object_not_found on a page the user can see
blockers.cause: Page wasn't shared with the integration in the picker.
blockers.next_step: Send the user back through authorisation to add pages, or ask them to add the connection on the page.

blockers.cause: redirect_uri missing from the token request when several are registered, or code reused.
blockers.next_step: Include redirect_uri in the token request; codes are single-use.

agent_can: Generate redirect URIs and the integration settings
Write the OAuth, refresh and 'page not shared' handling code
Draft in-product copy explaining the page picker
Probe the authorise endpoint and your callback
you_must: Sign in to Notion and create the integration

claims.claim: Authorisation works as soon as client credentials and redirect URI are configured; Marketplace submission/review is not required.
Installation scope (any workspace vs selected workspaces) cannot be changed after creation.
Token exchange returns access_token and refresh_token; refreshing returns a new pair.
claims.note: Checked 2026-11-03. Access token lifetime is not stated.

claims.claim: The authorise endpoint redirects to app.notion.com/install-integration without validating client_id server-side first.
claims.note: Probe with an all-zero client_id returned 302 to the install page.

claims.claim: Users choose pages in a picker; sharing a parent grants children.

open_questions: Access token lifetime is not documented on the authorisation page - confirm by observing expires_in in a real exchange.
Whether workspace admins can block public integrations on Enterprise plans was not checked.
